subject: car tire
title: What If You Never Checked Your Tire Pressure?

scenes.text: What if you never checked your tire pressure? Your tires would look fine. Until they didn't.
Every month, a typical tire quietly loses about 1 psi of air, even without a puncture.
Cold weather takes more: roughly another 1 psi for every 10 degree Fahrenheit drop in temperature.
After a year, that adds up, and each psi lost cuts your gas mileage by about zero point two percent.
Soft tires flex and build up extra heat, wearing the edges unevenly and raising the risk of a blowout.
In a federal crash study, tires 25 percent underinflated were three times as likely to have trouble before a crash.

description:
What if you never checked your tire pressure? Tires lose about 1 psi a month and roughly 1 psi per 10 degree F drop, and the US Department of Energy says each psi of underinflation costs about 0.2 percent of your gas mileage.
In NHTSA's crash causation study, tires underinflated by 25 percent or more were three times as likely to have problems before a crash.
